items.editor_note: Adds a continual-RL angle: replay guided by policy improvement, not only knowledge retention.

items.title: SUAF: Spectral Universal Advantage Features for Zero-Shot Policy Improvement
items.summary_1line: The paper proposes Spectral Universal Advantage Features (SUAF), reward-independent representations derived from an action-centered canonical dependence matrix, and reports finite-state and zero-shot evaluations on discrete and continuous-control tasks.
items.editor_note: Proposes reward-independent features for zero-shot policy improvement on control tasks.

items.title: CO-GRAFT: Attributing Reinforcement Learning Gains in Search Agents via Role-Level Policy Grafting
items.summary_1line: CO-GRAFT is a framework that attributes RL gains in Search-R1 search agents to four functional roles by mixing RL-trained and pre-RL policies, finding query generation contributes at most 15% of the gain.
items.editor_note: First agent-specific attribution result: query generation caps at 15% of Search-R1's RL gain.

editorial.tldr: This is a theme thread, not one event: six November items share the words "policy learning" or "policy improvement" across speech translation, multi-agent orchestration, robotics, and continual RL. Google's Gemini 4 Argon, framed partly around robot policy improvement, is the only product release in the set.
editorial.whats_new: CO-GRAFT (Nov 23) swaps RL-trained and pre-RL policies role by role in Search-R1 agents and finds query generation accounts for at most 15% of the RL gain.
editorial.why_it_matters: For agent builders, the useful strand is attribution: knowing which agent role RL actually improved tells you where to spend fine-tuning and eval effort.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before RL-tuning a whole search agent, ablate per role (query writing, reading, answering) to find which step the training actually improves.
